# [Tuesday 15 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/15/)

Before I was up, [my brother’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/236/) man came to tell me that my cozen, [Edward Pepys](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/342/), was dead, died at [Mrs. Turner’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/121/), for which [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and I are very sorry, and the more for that [his wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2531/) was the only handsome woman of our name.

So up and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where the greatest business was [Sir J. Minnes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2463/) and [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) against me for [Sir W. Warren’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1748/) contract for [masts](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5619/), to which I may go to my memorandum book to see what past, but came off with conquest, and my [Lord Barkely](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1055/) and [Mr. Coventry](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/) well convinced that we are well used.

So [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, and thither came to me [Mr. Mount](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/571/) and [Mr. Luellin](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/506/), I think almost foxed, and there dined with me and very merry as I could be, my mind being troubled to see things so ordered at the Board, though with no disparagement to me at all.

At dinner comes a messenger from [the Counter](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7071/) with an execution against me for the 30 _l._ 10 _s._, given the last verdict to [Field](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3815/). The man’s name is [Thomas](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13726/), of [the Poultry Counter](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/14098/). I sent [Griffin](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1529/) with him to [the Dolphin](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/922/), where Sir W. Batten was at dinner, and he being satisfied that I should pay the money, I did cause the money to be paid him, and Griffin to tell it out to him in the office. He offered to go along with me to [Sir R. Ford](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1347/), but I thought it not necessary, but let him go with it, he also telling me that there is never any receipt for it given, but I have good witness of the payment of it.

They being gone, Luellin having again told me by myself that [Deering](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7073/) is content to give me 50 _l._ if I can sell his [deals](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4992/) for him to [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/), not that I did ever offer to take it, or bid Luellin bargain for me with him, but did tacitly seem to be willing to do him what service I could in it, and expect his thanks, what he thought good.

Thence to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) by coach, by the way overtaking [Mr. Moore](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/340/), and took him into the coach to me, and there he could tell me nothing of [my Lord](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), how he stands as to his thoughts or respect to me, but concludes that though at present he may be angry yet he will come to be pleased again with me no doubt, and says that he do mind his business well, and keeps at Court.

So to White Hall, and there by order found some of the [Commissioners of Tangier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5243/) met, and my Lord Sandwich among the rest, to whom I bowed, but he shewed me very little if any countenance at all, which troubles me mightily.

Having soon done there, I took up Mr. Moore again and set him down at [Pauls](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/280/), by the way he proposed to me of a way of profit which perhaps may shortly be made by money by fines upon houses at [the Wardrobe](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/946/), but how I did not understand but left it to another discourse.

So homeward, calling upon [Mr. Fen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1637/), by [Sir G. Carteret’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1018/) desire, and did there shew him the bill of [Captain Taylor’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2214/) whereby I hope to get something justly.

Home and to my office, and there very late with Sir W. Warren upon very serious discourse, telling him how matters passed to-day, and in the close he and I did fall to talk very openly of the business of this office, and (if I was not a little too open to tell him my interest, which is my fault) he did give me most admirable advice, and such as do speak him a most able and worthy man, and understanding seven times more than ever I thought to be in him. He did particularly run over every one of the officers and commanders, and shewed me how I had reason to mistrust every one of them, either for their falsenesse or their over-great power, being too high to fasten a real friendship in, and did give me a common but a most excellent saying to observe in all my life. He did give it in rhyme, but the sense was this, that a man should treat every friend in his discourse and opening his mind to him as of one that may hereafter be his foe. He did also advise me how I should take occasion to make known to the world my case, and the pains that I take in my business, and above all to be sure to get a thorough knowledge in my employment, and to that add all the interest at Court that I can, which I hope I shall do.

He staid talking with me till almost 12 at night, and so good night, being sorry to part with him, and more sorry that he should have as far as [Wapping](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2469/) to walk to-night. So I to my Journall and so home, to supper and to bed.

# [Wednesday 16 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/16/)

Up, and with my head and heart full of my business, I to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and there all the morning, where among other things to my great content [Captain Taylor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2214/) brought me 40 _l._, the greater part of which I shall gain to myself after much care and pains out of his bill of freight, as I have at large set down in my book of Memorandums.

At noon to [the ’Change](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/) and there met with [Mr. Wood](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/615/) by design, and got out of him to my advantage a condition which I shall make good use of against [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) (vide my book of Memorandums touching the contract of [masts](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5619/) of [Sir W. Warren](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1748/) about which I have had so much trouble).

So [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner and then to the [Star Tavern](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1643/) hard by to our arbitration of [Mr. Bland’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5181/) business, and at it a great while, but I found no order like to be kept in our inquiry, and [Mr. Clerke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6856/), the other arbitrator, one so far from being fit (though able as to his trade of a merchant) to inquire and to take pains in searching out the truth on both sides, that we parted without doing anything, nor do I believe we shall at all ever attain to anything in it.

Then home and till 12 at night making up my accounts with great account of this day’s receipt of Captain Taylor’s money and some money reimbursed me which I have laid out on [Field’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3815/) business. So home with my mind in pretty good quiet, and to Supper and to bed.

# [Thursday 17 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/17/)

Up and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where we sat all the morning. At noon [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to my poor [wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and dined, and then by coach abroad to [Mrs. Turner’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/121/) where I have not been for many a day, and there I found her and her sister [Dike](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7192/) very sad for the death of [their brother](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/342/). After a little common expression of sorrow, Mrs. Turner told me that the trouble she would put me to was, to consult about getting an achievement prepared, [scutcheons](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7076/) were done already, to set over the door. So I did go out to [Mr. Smith’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7077/), where [my brother](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/236/) tells me the scutcheons are made, but he not being within, I went to [the Temple](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/131/), and there spent my time in a Bookseller’s shop, reading in a book of some [Embassages into Moscovia, &c.](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7078/), where was very good reading, and then to Mrs. Turner’s, and thither came Smith to me, with whom I did agree for 4 _l._ to make a handsome one, ell square within the frame. After he was gone I sat an houre talking of the suddennesse of his death within 7 days, and how by little and little death came upon him, neither he nor they thinking it would come to that. He died after a day’s raveing, through lightness in his head for want of sleep. [His lady](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2531/) did not know of his sickness, nor do they hear yet how she takes it.

Hence home, taking some books by the way in [Paul’s Churchyard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/821/) by coach to my office, where late doing business, and so home to supper and to bed.

# [Friday 18 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/18/)

Up, and after being ready and done several businesses with people, I took water (taking a dram of the bottle at the waterside) with a [gally](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7865/), the first that ever I had yet, and down to [Woolwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1675/), calling at [Ham Creeke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5267/), where I met [Mr. Deane](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5132/), and had a great deal of talke with him about business, and so to the [Ropeyarde](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5129/) and Docke, discoursing several things, and so back again and did the like at [Deptford](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1350/), and I find that it is absolutely necessary for me to do thus once a weeke at least all the yeare round, which will do me great good, and so home with great ease and content, especially out of the content which I met with in a book I bought yesterday, being a discourse of the state of Rome under the present Pope, [Alexander the 7th](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4893/), it being a very excellent piece. After eating something at [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), then to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where till night about business to dispatch. Among other people came [Mr. Primate](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7080/), the leather seller, in [Fleete Streete](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/127/), to see me, he says, coming this way; and he tells me that he is upon a proposal to [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/), whereby, by a law already in being, he will supply the King, without wrong to any man, or charge to the people in general, so much as it is now, above 200,000 _l._ per annum, and God knows what, and that the King do like the proposal, and hath directed that the [Duke of Monmouth](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5315/), with their consent, be made privy, and go along with him and his fellow proposer in the business, God knows what it is; for I neither can guess nor believe there is any such thing in his head. At night made an end of the discourse I read this morning, and so home to supper and to bed.

# [Saturday 19 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/19/)

Up and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where we sat all the morning, and I laboured hard at [Deering’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7073/) business of his [deals](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4992/) more than I would if I did not think to get something, though I do really believe that I did what is to [the King’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) advantage in it, and yet, God knows, the expectation of profit will have its force and make a man the more earnest. Dined at [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and then with [Mr. Bland](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5181/) to another meeting upon his arbitration, and seeing we were likely to do no good I even put them upon it, and they chose [Sir W. Rider](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1766/) alone to end the matter, and so I am rid of it. Thence by coach to my shoemaker’s and paid all there, and gave something to the boys’ box against [Christmas](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/314/). To [Mrs. Turner’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/121/), whom I find busy with [Sir W. Turner](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3725/), about advising upon going down to Norfolke with the corps, and I find him in talke a sober, considering man. So home to my office late, and then home to supper and to bed. My head full of business, but pretty good content.

# [Sunday 20 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/20/)

(Lord’s day). Up and alone to [church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/), where a common sermon of [Mr. Mills](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1215/), and so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner in our parler, [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) being clean, and the first time we have dined here a great while together, and in the afternoon went to church with me also, and there begun to take her place above [Mrs. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2849/), which heretofore out of a humour she was wont to give her as an affront to my [Lady Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1572/). After a dull sermon of [the Scotchman](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5805/), home, and there I found my brother [Tom](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/236/) and my two cozens Scotts, [he](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/951/) and [she](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1761/), the first time they were ever here. And by and by in comes my uncle [Wight](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/911/) and [Mr. Norbury](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2724/), and they sat with us a while drinking, of [wine](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/309/), of which I did give them plenty. But the two would not stay supper, but the other two did. And we were as merry as I could be with people that I do wish well to, but know not what discourse either to give them or find from them. We showed them our house from top to bottom, and had a good [Turkey](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/378/) roasted for our supper, and store of wine, and after supper sent them home on foot, and so we to prayers and to bed.

# [Monday 21 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/21/)

Up betimes, [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) having a mind to have gone abroad with me, but I had not because of troubling me, and so left her, though against my will, to go and see [her father](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1067/) and [mother](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1066/) by herself, and I straight to my [Lord Sandwich’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), and there I had a pretty kind salute from my Lord, and went on to [the Duke’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/), where my fellow [officers](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1121/) by and by came, and so in with him to his closet, and did our business, and so broke up, and I with [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) by coach to [Salisbury Court](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/161/), and there spoke with [Clerk](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5255/) our Solicitor about [Field’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3815/) business, and so parted, and I to [Mrs. Turner’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/121/), and there saw the achievement pretty well set up, and it is well done. Thence I on foot to [Charing Crosse](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/138/) to the [ordinary](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1199/), and there, dined, meeting [Mr. Gauden](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/994/) and [Creed](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/507/). Here variety of talk but to no great purpose. After dinner won a wager of a payre of [gloves](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/13924/) of a crowne of Mr. Gauden upon some words in his contract for [victualling](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9960/).

There parted in the street with them, and I to my Lord’s, but he not being within, took coach, and, being directed by sight of bills upon the walls, I did go to [Shoe Lane](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1095/) to see a [cocke-fighting](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7085/) at a new pit there, a sport I was never at in my life; but, Lord! to see the strange variety of people, from Parliament-man (by name [Wildes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7086/), that was Deputy Governor of [the Tower](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/167/) when [Robinson](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1156/) was [Lord Mayor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1522/)) to the poorest ’prentices, bakers, brewers, butchers, draymen, and what not; and all these fellows one with another in swearing, cursing, and betting. I soon had enough of it, and yet I would not but have seen it once, it being strange to observe the nature of these poor creatures, how they will fight till they drop down dead upon the table, and strike after they are ready to give up the ghost, not offering to run away when they are weary or wounded past doing further, whereas where a dunghill brood comes he will, after a sharp stroke that pricks him, run off the stage, and then they wring off his neck without more ado, whereas the other they preserve, though their eyes be both out, for breed only of a true cock of the game.

Sometimes a cock that has had ten to one against him will by chance give an unlucky blow, will strike the other starke dead in a moment, that he never stirs more; but the common rule is, that though a cock neither runs nor dies, yet if any man will bet 10 _l._ to a crowne, and nobody take the bet, the game is given over, and not sooner. One thing more it is strange to see how people of this poor rank, that look as if they had not bread to put in their mouths, shall bet three or four pounds at one bet, and lose it, and yet bet as much the next battle (so they call every match of two cocks), so that one of them will lose 10 _l._ or 20 _l._ at a meeting.

Thence, having enough of it, by coach to my Lord Sandwich’s, where I find him within with [Captain Cooke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1192/) and his boys, [Dr. Childe](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1253/), [Mr. Madge](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1198/), and [Mallard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1493/), playing and singing over my Lord’s anthem which he hath made to sing in the King’s Chappell: my Lord saluted me kindly and took me into the withdrawing-room, to hear it at a distance, and indeed it sounds very finely, and is a good thing, I believe, to be made by him, and they all commend it. And after that was done Captain Cooke and his two boys did sing some Italian songs, which I must in a word say I think was fully the best musique that I ever yet heard in all my life, and it was to me a very great pleasure to hear them.

After all musique ended, my Lord going to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/), I went along with him, and made a desire for to have his coach to go along with my cozen [Edward Pepys’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/342/) hearse through [the City](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/275/) on Wednesday next, which he granted me presently, though he cannot yet come to speak to me in the familiar stile that he did use to do, nor can I expect it. But I was the willinger of this occasion to see whether he would deny me or no, which he would I believe had he been at open defyance against me.

Being not a little pleased with all this, though I yet see my Lord is not right yet, I thanked his Lordship and parted with him in White Hall. I back to my Lord’s, and there took up [W. Howe](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/549/) in a coach, and carried him as far as the [Half Moone](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/957/), and there set him down. By the way, talking of my Lord, who is come another and a better man than he was lately, and God be praised for it, and he says that I shall find my Lord as he used to be to me, of which I have good hopes, but I shall beware of him, I mean W. Howe, how I trust him, for I perceive he is not so discreet as I took him for, for he has told [Captain Ferrers](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/727/) (as [Mr. Moore](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/340/) tells me) of my letter to my Lord, which troubles me, for fear my Lord should think that I might have told him.

So called with my coach at my wife’s [brother’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/631/) lodging, but she was gone newly in a coach homewards, and so I drove hard and overtook her at [Temple Bar](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/276/), and there paid off mine, and went [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) with her in her coach. She tells me how there is a sad house among her friends. Her brother’s [wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5735/) proves very unquiet, and so her mother is, gone back to be with her husband and leave the young couple to themselves, and great trouble, and I fear great want, will be among them, I pray keep me from being troubled with them.

At home to put on my gowne and to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and there set down this day’s Journall, and by and by comes [Mrs. Owen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7089/), [Captain Allen’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1330/) daughter, and causes me to stay while the papers relating to [her husband’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7088/) place, bought of his father, be copied out because of her going by this morning’s tide home to [Chatham](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/643/). Which vexes me, but there is no help for it. I home to supper while a young [man] that she brought with her did copy out the things, and then I to the office again and dispatched her, and so home to bed.

# [Tuesday 22 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/22/)

Up and there comes my she cozen [Angier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/14062/), of [Cambridge](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2589/), to me to speak about [her son](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6367/). But though I love them, and have reason so to do, yet, Lord! to consider how cold I am to speak to her, for fear of giving her too much hopes of expecting either money or anything else from me besides my care of her son. I let her go without drinking, though that was against my will, being forced to hasten to the office, where we sat all the morning, and at noon I to [Sir R. Ford’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1347/), where [Sir R. Browne](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3795/) (a dull but it seems upon action a hot man), and he and I met upon setting a price upon the freight of a barge sent to France to the [Duchess of Orleans](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1272/). And here by discourse I find them greatly crying out against the choice of [Sir J. Cutler](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5851/) to be Treasurer for [Paul’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/280/) upon condition that he give 1500 _l._ towards it, and it seems he did give it upon condition that he might be Treasurer for the work, which they say will be worth three times as much money, and talk as if his being chosen to the office will make people backward to give, but I think him as likely a man as either of them, or better.

The business being done we parted, Sir R. Ford never inviting me to dine with him at all, and I was not sorry for it.

[Home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and dined. I had a letter from [W. Howe](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/549/) that [my Lord](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/) hath ordered his coach and six horses for me to-morrow, which pleases me mightily to think that my Lord should do so much, hoping thereby that his anger is a little over.

After dinner abroad with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) by coach to Westminster, and set her at [Mrs. Hunt’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/240/) while I about my business, having in our way met with [Captain Ferrers](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/727/) luckily to speak to him about my coach, who was going in all haste thither, and I perceive [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) and [Duke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) and all the Court was going to the [Duke’s playhouse](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2935/) to see [“Henry VIII.”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7044/) acted, which is said to be an admirable play. But, Lord! to see how near I was to have broken my oathe, or run the hazard of 20 _s._ losse, so much my nature was hot to have gone thither; but I did not go, but having spoke with W. Howe and known how my Lord did do this kindly as I would have it, I did go to [Westminster Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/128/), and there met [Hawley](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/208/), and walked a great while with him. Among other discourse encouraging him to pursue his love to [Mrs. Lane](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1157/), while God knows I had a roguish meaning in it.

Thence calling my wife home by coach, calling at several places, and to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where late, and so home to supper and to bed.

This day I hear for certain that my [Lady Castlemaine](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1062/) is turned [Papist](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/306/), which [the Queene](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2381/) for all do not much like, thinking that she do it not for conscience sake.

I heard to-day of a great fray lately between [Sir H. Finch’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1176/) coachman, who struck with his whip a coachman of the King’s to the losse of one of his eyes; at which the people of [the Exchange](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/) seeming to laugh and make sport with some words of contempt to him, my [Lord Chamberlin](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/671/) did come from the King to shut up the ’Change, and by the help of a justice, did it; but upon petition to the King it was opened again.

# [Wednesday 23 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/23/)

Up betimes and [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/); and being in as mourning a dress as we could, at present, without cost, put ourselves into, we by [Sir W. Pen’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) coach to [Mrs. Turner’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/121/), at [Salisbury Court](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/161/), where I find [my Lord’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/) coach and six horses. We staid till almost eleven o’clock, and much company came, and anon, the corps being put into the hearse, and the [scutcheons](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7076/) set upon it, we all took coach, and I and my wife and [Auditor Beale](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5699/) in my Lord Sandwich’s coach, and went next to Mrs. Turner’s mourning coach, and so through all [the City](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/275/) and [Shoreditch](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7093/), I believe about twenty coaches, and four or five with six and four horses.

Being come thither, I made up to the mourners, and bidding them a good journey, I took leave and back again, and setting my wife into [a hackney](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/575/) out of [Bishopsgate Street](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2191/), I sent her [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and I to [the ’Change](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/) and Auditor Beale about his business.

Did much business at the ’Change, and so home to dinner, and then to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and there late doing business also to my great content to see God bless me in my place and opening honest ways, I hope to get a little money to lay up and yet to live handsomely. So to supper and to bed. My wife having strange fits of the toothache, some times on this, and by and by on that side of her tooth, which is not common.

[Read 31 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/23/#annotations)

# [Thursday 24 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/24/)

Up betimes; and though it was a most foggy morning, and cold, yet with a [gally](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7865/) down to [Eriffe](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2697/), several times being at a loss whither we went. There I mustered [two](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3664/)[ships](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7104/) of [the King’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/), lent by him to [the Guiny Company](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7105/), which are manned better than ours at far less wages. Thence on board two of the King’s, one of them the [“Leopard,”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7106/)[Captain Beech](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7107/), who I find an able and serious man. He received me civilly, and his wife was there, a very well bred and knowing woman, born at [Antwerp](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7108/), but speaks as good English as myself, and an ingenious woman. Here was also [Sir G. Carteret’s son](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7109/), who I find a pretty, but very talking man, but good humour.

Thence back again, entertaining myself upon my [sliding rule](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6104/) with great content, and called at [Woolwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1675/), where [Mr. Chr. Pett](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1809/) having an opportunity of being alone did tell me his mind about several things he thought I was offended with him in, and told me of my kindness to [his assistant](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5132/). I did give him such an answer as I thought was fit and left him well satisfied, he offering to do me all the service, either by draughts or modells that I should desire. Thence straight [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), being very cold, but yet well, I thank God, and at home found [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) making [mince pies](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3371/), and by and by comes in [Captain Ferrers](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/727/) to see us, and, among other talke, tells us of the goodness of the new play of [“Henry VIII.,”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7044/) which makes me think [it] long till my time is out; but I hope before I go I shall set myself such a stint as I may not forget myself as I have hitherto done till I was forced for these months last past wholly to forbid myself the seeing of one.

He gone I to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) and there late writing and reading, and so home to bed.

# [Friday 25 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/25/)

([Christmas day](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/314/)). Lay long talking pleasantly with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/), but among other things she begun, I know not whether by design or chance, to enquire what she should do if I should by any accident die, to which I did give her some slight answer; but shall make good use of it to bring myself to some settlement for her sake, by making a will as soon as I can.

Up and to [church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/), where [Mr. Mills](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1215/) made an ordinary sermon, and so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and dined with great pleasure with my wife, and all the afternoon first looking out at window and seeing the boys playing at many several sports in our back yard by [Sir W. Pen’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/), which reminded me of my own former times, and then I began to read to my wife upon the [globes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6732/) with great pleasure and to good purpose, for it will be pleasant to her and to me to have her understand these things.

In the evening at [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where I staid late reading [Rushworth](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7002/), which is a most excellent collection of the beginning of the late quarrels in this kingdom, and so home to supper and to bed, with good content of mind.

[Read 18 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/25/#annotations)

# [Saturday 26 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/26/)

Up and walked forth first to the [Minerys](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6103/) to [Brown’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6102/), and there with great pleasure saw and bespoke several instruments, and so to [Cornhill](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1608/) to [Mr. Cades](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5737/), and there went up into his warehouse to look for a map or two, and there finding great plenty of good pictures, God forgive me! how my mind run upon them, and bought a little one for [my wife’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) closett presently, and concluded presently of buying 10 _l._ worth, upon condition he would give me the buying of them. Now it is true I did still within me resolve to make [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) one way or other pay for them, though I saved it to him another way, yet I find myself too forward to fix upon the expense, and came away with a resolution of buying them, but do hope that I shall not upon second thoughts do it without a way made out before I buy them to myself how to do [it] without charge to my main stock. Thence to [the Coffee-house](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/813/), and sat long in good discourse with some gentlemen concerning the Roman Empire. So [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and found [Mr. Hollyard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1536/) there, and he stayed and dined with us, we having a [pheasant](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7110/) to dinner. He gone, I all the afternoon with my wife to [cards](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/797/), and, God forgive me! to see how the very discourse of plays, which I shall be at liberty to see after New Year’s Day next, do set my mind upon them, but I must be forced to stint myself very strictly before I begin, or else I fear I shall spoil all.

In the evening came my [aunt Wight’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/995/)[kinswoman](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7167/) to see how my wife do, with a compliment from my aunt, which I take kindly as it is unusual for her to do it, but I do perceive [my uncle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/911/) is very kind to me of late.

So to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) writing letters, and then to read and make an end of [Rushworth](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7002/), which I did, and do say that it is a book the most worth reading for a man of my condition or any man that hopes to come to any publique condition in the world that I do know.

So home to supper and to bed.

[Read 15 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/26/#annotations)

# [Sunday 27 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/27/)

Up and to [church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/) alone and so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) very pleasant and pleased with one another’s company, and in our general enjoyment one of another, better we think than most other couples do. So after dinner to the [French church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5696/), but came too late, and so back to our owne church, where I slept all the sermon [the Scott](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5805/) preaching, and so home, and in the evening [Sir J. Minnes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2463/) and I met at [Sir W. Pen’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) about ordering some business of the Navy, and so I home to supper, discourse, prayers, and bed.

[Read 18 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/27/#annotations)

# [Monday 28 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/28/)

Up and by coach to [my Lord’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/) lodgings, but he was gone abroad, so I lost my pains, but, however, walking through [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) I heard [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) was gone to play at [Tennis](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1644/), so I down to the new [Tennis Court](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7117/); and saw him and [Sir Arthur Slingsby](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6657/) play against my [Lord of Suffolke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2521/) and my [Lord Chesterfield](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/164/). The King beat three, and lost two sets, they all, and he particularly playing well, I thought. Thence went and spoke with the [Duke of Albemarle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/111/) about his wound at [Newhall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7118/), but I find him a heavy dull man, methinks, by his answers to me. Thence to the [King’s Head](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1110/)[ordinary](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1199/) and there dined, and found [Creed](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/507/) there, but we met and dined and parted without any thing more than “How do you?” After dinner straight on foot to [Mr. Hollyard’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1536/), and there paid him 3 _l._ in full for his physic and work to [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) … [about her evill below; – L&M] but whether it is cured for ever or no I cannot tell, but he says it will never come to anything, though it may be it may ooze now and then a little. So [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and found my wife gone out with [Will](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1082/) (whom she sent for as she do now a days upon occasion) to have a tooth drawn, she having it seems been in great pain all day, and at night came home with it drawn, and pretty well. This evening I had a stove brought me to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) to try, but it being an old one it smokes as much as if there was nothing but a hearth as I had before, but it may be great new ones do not, and therefore I must enquire further. So at night home to supper and to bed.

The [Duchesse of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1402/) is fallen sicke of the meazles.

[Read 19 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/28/#annotations)

# [Tuesday 29 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/29/)

Up and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where all the morning sitting, at noon to [the ‘change](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/), and there I found and brought [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/)[Mr. Pierse](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/173/) the surgeon to dinner. Where I found also [Mr. Luellin](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/506/) and [Mount](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/571/), and merry at dinner, but their discourse so free … [about claps and other foul discourse – L&M] that I was weary of them. But after dinner Luellin took me up to my chamber to give me 50 _l._ for the service I did him, though not so great as he expected and I intended. But I told him that I would not sell my liberty to any man. If he would give me any thing by another’s hand I would endeavour to deserve it, but I will never give him himself thanks for it, not acknowledging the receiving of any, which he told me was reasonable. I did also tell him that neither this nor any thing should make me to do any thing that should not be for [the King’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) service besides. So we parted and left them three at home with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) going to [cards](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/797/), and I to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) and there staid late.

[Sir W. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) came like a cunning rogue to sit and talk with me about office business and freely about the [Comptroller’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2463/) business of the office, to which I did give him free answers and let him make the best of them. But I know him to be a knave, and do say nothing that I fear to have said again.

Anon came [Sir W. Warren](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1748/), and after talking of his business of the [masts](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5619/) and helping me to understand some foul dealing in the business of [Woods](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/615/) we fell to other talk, and particularly to speak of some means how to part this great familiarity between [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) and [Sir J. Minnes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2463/), and it is easy to do by any good friend of Sir J. Minnes to whom it will be a good service, and he thinks that [Sir J. Denham](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1676/) will be a proper man for it, and so do I. So after other discourse we parted, and I home and to bed.

[Read 22 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/29/#annotations)

# [Wednesday 30 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/30/)

Up betimes and by coach to my [Lord Sandwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), who I met going out, and he did aske me how his cozen, [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/); did, the first time he hath done so since his being offended, and, in my conscience, he would be glad to be free with me again, but he knows not how to begin. So he went out, and I through the garden to [Mr. Coventry](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/), where I saw [Mr. Ch. Pett](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1809/) bringing him a modell, and indeed it is a pretty one, for a New Year’s gift; but I think the work not better done than mine.

With him by coach to [London](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/275/), with good and friendly discourse of business and against [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) and his foul dealings. So leaving him at the [Guiny House](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7006/) I to the [Coffee House](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/813/), whither came [Mr. Grant](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2630/) and [Sir W. Petty](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1020/), with whom I talked, and so did many, almost all the house there, about his [new vessel](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4001/), wherein he did give me such satisfaction in every point that I am almost confident she will prove an admirable invention.

So home to dinner, and after being upon [the ’Change](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/) awhile I dined with my wife, who took physique to-day, and so to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and there all the afternoon till late at night about office business, and so to supper and to bed.

# [Thursday 31 December 1663](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1663/12/31/)

Up and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where we sat all the morning, and among other things [Sir W. Warren](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1748/) came about some contract, and there did at the open table, [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) not being there; openly defy him, and insisted how Sir W. Batten did endeavour to oppose him in everything that he offered. [Sir W. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/) took him up for it, like a counterfeit rogue, though I know he was as much pleased to hear him talk so as any man there. But upon his speaking no more was said but to the business. At noon we broke up and I to [the ’Change](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/) awhile, and so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) again to dinner, my head aching mightily with being overcharged with business. We had to dinner, [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and I, a fine [turkey](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/378/) and a [mince pie](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3371/), and dined in state, poor wretch, she and I, and have thus kept our [Christmas](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/314/) together all alone almost, having not once been out, but to-morrow my vowes are all out as to plays and [wine](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/309/), but I hope I shall not be long before I come to new ones, so much good, and God’s blessing, I find to have attended them. Thence to the office and did several businesses and answered several people, but my head aching and it being my great night of accounts, I went forth, took coach, and to [my brother’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/236/), but he was not within, and so I back again and sat an hour or two at the [Coffee [house]](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/813/), hearing some simple discourse about [Quakers](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/305/) being charmed by a string about their wrists, and so home, and after a little while at my office, I home and supped, and so had a good fire in my chamber and there sat till 4 o’clock in the morning making up my accounts and writing this last Journall of the year. And first I bless God I do, after a large expense, even this month, by reason of Christmas, and some payments to [my father](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/154/), and other things extraordinary, find that I am worth in money, besides all my household stuff, or any thing of [Brampton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1768/), [above 800 _l._](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9548/), whereof in my [Lord Sandwich’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/) hand, 700 _l._, and the rest in my hand. So that there is not above 5 _l._ of all my estate in money at this minute out of my hands and my Lord’s. For which the good God be pleased to give me a thankful heart and a mind careful to preserve this and increase it.

I do live at my lodgings in the Navy Office, my family being, besides my wife and I, [Jane Gentleman](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6655/), [Besse](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6788/), our excellent, good-natured cookmayde, and [Susan](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6687/), a little girle, having neither man nor boy, nor like to have again a good while, living now in most perfect content and quiett, and very frugally also; my health pretty good, but only that I have been much troubled with a costiveness which I am labouring to get away, and have hopes of doing it. At the office I am well, though envied to the devil by Sir William Batten, who hates me to death, but cannot hurt me. The rest either love me, or at least do not show otherwise, though I know Sir W. Pen to be a false knave touching me, though he seems fair.

My father and [mother](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/282/) well in the country; and at this time the young ladies of [Hinchingbroke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/104/) with them, their house having the [small-pox](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/363/) in it.

[The Queene](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2381/) after a long and sore sicknesse is become well again; and [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) minds his mistresse a little too much, if it pleased God! but I hope all things will go well, and in the Navy particularly, wherein I shall do my duty whatever comes of it.

The great talke is the designs of the [King of France](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5855/), whether against [the Pope](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4893/) or [King of Spayne](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6888/) nobody knows; but a great and a most promising Prince he is, and all the Princes of Europe have their eye upon him. [My wife’s brother](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/631/) come to great unhappiness by the ill-disposition, my wife says, of [his wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5735/), and her poverty, which she now professes, after all her husband’s pretence of a great fortune, but I see none of them, at least they come not to trouble me.

At present I am concerned for my cozen [Angier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2804/), of [Cambridge](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2589/), lately broke in his trade, and this day am sending his son [John](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6367/), a very rogue, to sea.

My brother [Tom](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/236/) I know not what to think of, for I cannot hear whether he minds his business or not; and my brother [John](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/117/) at Cambridge, with as little hopes of doing good there, for when he was here he did give me great cause of dissatisfaction with his manner of life. [Pall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1568/) with my father, and God knows what she do there, or what will become of her, for I have not anything yet to spare her, and she grows now old, and must be disposed of one way or other.

The [Duchesse of York](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1402/), at this time, sicke of the [meazles](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7119/), but is growing well again.

[The Turke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6903/) very far entered into Germany, and all that part of the world at a losse what to expect from his proceedings.

Myself, blessed be God! in a good way, and design and resolution of sticking to my business to get a little money with doing the best service I can to the King also; which God continue! So ends the old year.

# Diary entries from December 1664

# [Thursday 1 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/01/)

Up betimes and to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) to a [Committee of Tangier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5243/), and so straight [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) and hard to my business at [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) till noon, then to dinner, and so to my office, and by and by we sat all the afternoon, then to my office again till past one in the morning, and so home to supper and to bed.

# [Friday 2 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/02/)

Lay long in bed. Then up and to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where busy all the morning. At [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) dined. After dinner with [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and [Mercer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7761/) to the [Duke’s House](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2935/), and there saw [“The Rivalls,”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7862/) which I had seen before; but the play not good, nor anything but the good actings of [Betterton](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2307/) and [his wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4034/) and [Harris](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6533/).

Thence homeward, and the coach broke with us in [Lincoln’s Inn Fields](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/125/), and so walked to [Fleete Streete](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/127/), and there took coach and home, and to my office, whither by and by comes [Captain Cocke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3164/), and then [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/), and we all to [Sir J. Minnes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2463/), and I did give them a barrel of [oysters](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/373/) I had given to me, and so there sat and talked, where good discourse of the late troubles, they knowing things, all of them, very well; and Cocke, from [the King’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/624/) own mouth, being then entrusted himself much, do know particularly that the King’s credulity to [Cromwell’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/796/) promises, private to him, against the advice of his friends and the certain discovery of the practices and discourses of Cromwell in council (by [Major Huntington](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8076/)) did take away his life and nothing else.1

Then to some loose atheisticall discourse of Cocke’s, when he was almost drunk, and then about 11 o’clock broke up, and I to my office, to fit up an account for Povy, wherein I hope to get something. At it till almost two o’clock, then to supper and to bed.

1.   According to Clarendon the officer here alluded to was a major in Cromwell’s own regiment of horse, and employed by him to treat with Charles I. whilst at Hampton Court; but being convinced of the insincerity of the proceeding, communicated his suspicions to that monarch, and immediately gave up his commission. We hear no more of Huntington till the Restoration, when his name occurs with those of many other officers, who tendered their services to the king. His reasons for laying down his commission are printed in Thurloe’s “State Papers” and Maseres’s “Tracts.” — B. ↩

# [Saturday 3 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/03/)

Up, and at [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) all the morning, and at noon to [Mr. Cutler’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4966/), and there dined with [Sir W. Rider](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1766/) and him, and thence Sir W. Rider and I by coach to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) to a Committee of [the Fishery](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7696/); there only to hear [Sir Edward Ford’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6773/) proposal about farthings, wherein, O God! to see almost every body interested for him; only my [Lord Annesly](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/887/), who is a grave, serious man. My [Lord Barkeley](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1055/) was there, but is the most hot, fiery man in discourse, without any cause, that ever I saw, even to breach of civility to my Lord Anglesey, in his discourse opposing to my Lord’s. At last, though without much satisfaction to me, it was voted that it should be requested of [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/), and that Sir Edward Ford’s proposal is the best yet made. Thence by coach [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/). The [Duke of Yorke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) being expected to-night with great joy from [Portsmouth](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1764/), after his having been abroad at sea three or four days with the fleete; and the Dutch are all drawn into their harbours. But it seems like a victory: and a matter of some reputation to us it is, and blemish to them; but in no degree like what it is esteemed at, the weather requiring them to do so. Home and at my office late, and then to supper and to bed.

# [Sunday 4 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/04/)

(Lord’s day). Lay long in bed, and then up and to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), there to dispatch a business in order to the getting something out of the [Tangier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2783/) business, wherein I have an opportunity to get myself paid upon the score of freight. I hope a good sum.

At noon [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, and then in the afternoon to [church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/). So home, and by and by comes [Mr. Hill](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7165/) and [Andrews](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7673/), and sung together long and with great content. Then to supper and broke up. Pretty discourse, very pleasant and ingenious, and so to my office a little, and then home (after prayers) to bed.

This day I hear the [Duke of Yorke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) is come to towne, though expected last night, as I observed, but by what hindrance stopped I can’t tell.

# [Monday 5 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/05/)

Up, and to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) with [Sir J. Minnes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2463/); and there, among an infinite crowd of great persons, did kiss [the Duke’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) hand; but had no time to discourse. Thence up and down the gallery, and got my [Lord of Albemarle’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/111/) hand to my bill for [Povy](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5263/), but afterwards was asked some scurvy questions by Povy about my demands, which troubled [me], but will do no great hurt I think. Thence vexed [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and there by appointment comes my cozen [Roger Pepys](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/247/) and [Mrs. Turner](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/121/), and dined with me, and very merry we were. They staid all the afternoon till night, and then after I had discoursed an hour with [Sir W. Warren](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1748/) plainly declaring my resolution to desert him if he goes on to join with [Castle](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2461/), who and his family I, for great provocation, love not, which he takes with some trouble, but will concur in everything with me, he says. Now I am loth, I confess, to lose him, he having been the best friend I have had ever in this office. So he being gone, we all, it being night, in Madam Turner’s coach to her house, there to see, as she tells us, how fat [Mrs. The.](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/120/) is grown, and so I find her, but not as I expected, but mightily pleased I am to hear the mother commend her daughter [Betty](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8086/) that she is like to be a great beauty, and she sets much by her.

Thence I to White Hall, and there saw [Mr. Coventry](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/) come to towne, and, with all my heart, am glad to see him, but could have no talke with him, he being but just come. Thence back and took up [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/), and home, where a while, and then home to supper and to bed.

# [Tuesday 6 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/06/)

Up, and in [Sir W. Batten’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) coach to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/), but [the Duke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) being gone forth, I to [Westminster Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/128/), and there spent much time till towards noon to and fro with people. So by and by [Mrs. Lane](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1157/) comes and plucks me by the cloak to speak to me, and I was fain to go to her shop, and pretending to buy some [bands](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5633/) made her go home, and by and by followed her, and there did what I would with her, and so after many discourses and her intreating me to do something for [her husband](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7729/), which I promised to do, and buying a little band of her, which I intend to keep to, I took leave, there coming a couple of footboys to her with a coach to fetch her abroad I know not to whom. She is great with child, and she says I must be godfather, but I do not intend it. Thence by coach to the [Old Exchange](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/), and there hear that the Dutch are fitting their ships out again, which puts us to new discourse, and to alter our thoughts of the Dutch, as to their want of courage or force. Thence by appointment to the [White Horse Taverne](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8054/) in [Lumbard Streete](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/966/), and there dined with my [Lord Rutherford](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5728/), [Povy](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5263/), [Mr. Gauden](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/994/), [Creed](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/507/), and others, and very merry, and after dinner among other things Povy and I withdrew, and I plainly told him that I was concerned in profit, but very justly, in this business of the Bill that I have been these two or three days about, and he consents to it, and it shall be paid.

He tells me how he believes, and in part knows, Creed to be worth 10,000 _l._; nay, that now and then he [Povy] hath three or 4,000 _l._ in his hands, for which he gives the interest that [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) gives, which is ten per cent., and that Creed do come and demand it every three months the interest to be paid him, which Povy looks upon as a cunning and mean tricke of him; but for all that, he will do and is very rich. Thence to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where we sat and where [Mr. Coventry](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/) came the first time after his return from sea, which I was glad of.

So after office to my office, and then [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to supper, and to my office again, and then late home to bed.

[Read 21 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/06/#annotations)

# [Wednesday 7 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/07/)

Lay long, then up, and among others [Bagwell’s wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6480/) coming to speak with me put new thoughts of folly into me which I am troubled at. Thence after doing business at [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), I by coach to my [Lady Sandwich’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/115/), and there dined with her, and found all well and merry. Thence to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/), and we waited on [the Duke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/), who looks better than he did, methinks, before his voyage; and, I think, a little more stern than he used to do.

Thence to [the Temple](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/131/) to my cozen [Roger Pepys](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/247/), thinking to have met the Doctor to have discoursed our business, but he came not, so I [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and there by agreement came my [Lord Rutherford](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5728/), [Povy](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5263/), [Gauden](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/994/), [Creed](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/507/), [Alderman Backewell](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/967/), about [Tangier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2783/) business of accounts between Rutherford and Gauden. Here they were with me an hour or more, then after drinking away, and Povy and Creed staid and eat with me; but I was sorry I had no better cheer for Povy; for the foole may be useful, and is a cunning fellow in his way, which is a strange one, and that, that I meet not in any other man, nor can describe in him. They late with me, and when gone [my boy](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7767/) and I to musique, and then to bed.

[Read 15 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/07/#annotations)

# [Thursday 8 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/08/)

Up, and to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where all the morning busy. At noon dined at [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and then to the office, where we sat all the afternoon. In the evening comes my [aunt](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/995/) and [uncle Wight](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/911/), [Mrs. Norbury](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2725/), and her daughter, and after them [Mr. Norbury](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2724/), where no great pleasure, my aunt being out of humour in her fine clothes, and it raining hard. Besides, I was a little too bold with her about her doating on [Dr. Venner](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8087/). Anon they went away, and I till past 12 at night at my office, and then home to bed.

[Read 11 annotations by readers](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/08/#annotations)

# [Friday 9 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/09/)

Up betimes and walked to [Mr. Povy’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5263/), and there, not without some few troublesome questions of his, I got a note, and went and received 117 _l._ 5 _s._ of [Alderman Viner](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7169/) upon my pretended freight of the [“William”](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8088/) for [Tangier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2783/), which overbears me on one side with joy and on the other to think of my condition if I shall be called into examination about it, and (though in strictness it is due) not be able to give a good account of it.

[Home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) with it, and there comes [Captain Taylor](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2214/) to me, and he and I did set even the business of the ship [Union](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8089/) lately gone for Tangier, wherein I hope to get 50 _l._ more, for all which the Lord be praised.

At noon home to dinner, [Mr. Hunt](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/239/) and [his wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/240/) with us, and very pleasant. Then in the afternoon I carried them home by coach, and I to [Westminster Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/128/), and thence to [Gervas’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6230/), and there find I cannot prevail with [Jane](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7853/) to go forth with me, but though I took a good occasion of going to the [Trumpet](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1158/) she declined coming, which vexed me. ‘Je avait grande envie envers elle, avec vrai amour et passion’.

Thence home and to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) till one in the morning, setting to rights in writing this day’s two accounts of Povy and Taylor, and then quietly to bed.

This day I had several letters from several places, of our bringing in great numbers of Dutch ships.

# [Saturday 10 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/10/)

Lay long, at which I am ashamed, because of so many people observing it that know not how late I sit up, and for fear of [Sir W. Batten’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) speaking of it to others, he having staid for me a good while. At [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/) all the morning, where comes my [Lord Brunkard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4135/) with his patent in his hand, and delivered it to [Sir J. Minnes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2463/) and myself, we alone being there all the day, and at noon I in his coach with him to [the ’Change](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/), where he set me down; a modest civil person he seems to be, but wholly ignorant in the business of the Navy as possible, but I hope to make a friend of him, being a worthy man.

Thence after hearing the great newes of so many Dutchmen being brought in to [Portsmouth](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1764/) and elsewhere, which it is expected will either put them upon present revenge or despair, I with [Sir W. Rider](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1766/) and [Cutler](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4966/) to dinner all alone to the [Great James](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2190/), where good discourse, and, I hope, occasion of getting something hereafter.

After dinner to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/) to the [Fishery](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7696/), where [the Duke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/) was with us.

So [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and late at [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), writing many letters, then home to supper and to bed. Yesterday come home, and this night I visited [Sir W. Pen](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/619/), who dissembles great respect and love to me, but I understand him very well.

[Major Holmes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/930/) is come from [Guinny](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6917/), and is now at [Plymouth](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5849/) with great wealth, they say.

# [Sunday 11 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/11/)

(Lord’s day). Up and to [church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1214/) alone in the morning. Dined at [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), mighty pleasantly. In the afternoon I to the [French church](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5696/), where much pleased with the three sisters of [the parson](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8090/), very handsome, especially in their noses, and sing prettily. I heard a good sermon of [the old man](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5747/), touching duty to parents. Here was [Sir Samuel Morland](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/779/) and [his lady](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8091/) very fine, with two footmen in new liverys (the church taking much notice of them), and going into their coach after sermon with great gazeing. So I [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), and my cozen, [Mary Pepys’s husband](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/6750/), comes after me, and told me that out of the money he received some months since he did receive 18 _d._ too much, and did now come and give it me, which was very pretty. So home, and there found [Mr. Andrews](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7673/) and [his lady](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8645/), a well-bred and a tolerable pretty woman, and by and by [Mr. Hill](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7165/) and to singing, and then to supper, then to sing again, and so good night. To prayers and tonight [bed].

It is a little strange how these [Psalms](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8056/) of [Ravenscroft](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8055/) after 2 or 3 times singing prove but the same again, though good. No diversity appearing at all almost.

# [Monday 12 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/12/)

Up, and with [Sir W. Batten](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/852/) by coach to [White Hall](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/180/), where all of us with [the Duke](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/800/); [Mr. Coventry](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/830/) privately did tell me the reason of his advice against our pretences to the [Prize Office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8052/) (in his letter from Portsmouth), because he knew that the King and the Duke had resolved to put in some Parliament men that have deserved well, and that would needs be obliged, by putting them in.

Thence homeward, called at [my bookseller’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1539/) and bespoke some books against the year’s out, and then to [the ’Change](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/), and so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, and then to [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), where my [Lord Brunkard](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4135/) comes and reads over part of our Instructions in the Navy — and I expounded it to him, so he is become my disciple. He gone, comes [Cutler](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4966/) to tell us that the [King of France](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5855/) hath forbid any canvass to be carried out of his kingdom, and I to examine went with him to the [East India house](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2492/) to see a letter, but came too late. So home again, and there late till 12 at night at my office, and then home to supper and to bed.

This day (to see how things are ordered in the world), I had a command from the [Earle of Sandwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), at [Portsmouth](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1764/), not to be forward with [Mr. Cholmly](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5179/) and [Sir J. Lawson](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/110/) about the [Mole](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/5384/) at [Tangier](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2783/), because that what I do therein will (because of his friendship to me known) redound against him, as if I had done it upon his score. So I wrote to my Lord my mistake, and am contented to promise never to pursue it more, which goes against my mind with all my heart.

# [Tuesday 13 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/13/)

Lay long in bed, then up, and many people to speak with me. Then to [my office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), and dined at noon at [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/), then to the office again, where we sat all the afternoon, and then home at night to a little supper, and so after my office again at 12 at night home to bed.

# [Wednesday 14 December 1664](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1664/12/14/)

Up, and after a while at [the office](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/483/), I abroad in several places, among others to [my bookseller’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1539/), and there spoke for several books against New Year’s day, I resolving to lay out about 7 _l._ or 8 _l._, God having given me some profit extraordinary of late; and bespoke also some [plate](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7982/), spoons, and forks. I pray God keep me from too great expenses, though these will still be pretty good money. Then to [the ’Change](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/189/), and I [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1023/) to dinner, where [Creed](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/507/) and [Mr. Caesar](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8104/), [my boy’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/7767/)[lute](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/540/) master, who plays indeed mighty finely, and after dinner I abroad, parting from Creed, and away to and fro, laying out or preparing for laying out more money, but I hope and resolve not to exceed therein, and to-night spoke for some fruit for the country for [my father](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/154/) against [Christmas](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/314/), and where should I do it, but at the pretty woman’s, that used to stand at the doore in [Fanchurch Streete](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1075/), I having a mind to know her.

So home, and late at my office, evening reckonings with [Shergoll](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8105/), hoping to get money by the business, and so away home to supper and to bed, not being very well through my taking cold of late, and so troubled with some wind.
